parole.significato: An annual herb, of species Lamium amplexicaule, with pink or purple flowers and deeply crenate leaves.
parole.testo: Calque of Dutch hoenderbeet. By surface analysis, hen + bit (past participle of bite; bitten). First attested in 1578. Cognate with Middle Low German hennebit and German Hühnerbiss; all likely derived from Medieval Latin Morsus gallinae, the ancestor of Italian mordigallina, French morgeline and obs

parole.significato: The chief provincial magistrate, military commander, and, as a member of the House of Orange, highest-ranking noble in…
parole.testo: Partial calque of Dutch stadthouder (superseded), stadhouder (literally “placeholder”), from Middle Dutch stathouder, itself a calque of Medieval Latin locum tenēns. Doublet of locum tenens and lieutenant.

parole.significato: A large drinking vessel, sometimes of pewter, sometimes with a glass base, with one handle and often a hinged cover.
parole.testo: From Middle English tan(c)kard(e), denoting 'a large tub for carrying liquid', perhaps related to Dutch tanckaert, from Middle Dutch tanckaert, meaning the same thing, but of uncertain ultimate origin. The OED suggests an alteration of Medieval Latin *kantard, from Latin cantharus (“tankard”). Klein
